blocks.prompt: 10. Let \(f\) be continuous, and suppose: \(\int_{1}^{3} f(x)\,dx = 8\). If the average value of \(f\) on \([1, 4]\) is three times the average value on \([3, 4]\), find \(\int_{3}^{4} f(x)\,dx\).
blocks.explanation:
Same idea as Q9: average = integral \(\div\) length.
Plan: call \(I = \int_3^4 f\); then \(\int_1^4 f = 8 + I\); write both averages and use "three times".
steps:
The two averages
\[f_{\text{av}}[1, 4] = \dfrac{8 + I}{4 - 1} = \dfrac{8 + I}{3}\]
\[f_{\text{av}}[3, 4] = \dfrac{I}{4 - 3} = I\]
Why: the lengths are 3 and 1.

Check
\(\int_1^4 f = 9\), average \(= 3\); average on \([3, 4]\) \(= 1\), and \(3 = 3 \times 1\;\checkmark\).
